episodes.about: AI capabilities are improving fast. But will the economy move just as quickly? a16z General Partner Erik Torenberg sits down with Google DeepMind economist Alex Imas and economist Tyler Cowen to examine how advances in AI translate into growth, jobs, wages, and productivity. They debate what it would take to reach double-digit economic growth, why bottlenecks and falling AI costs could slow the impact, and whether frontier lab valuations require much larger productivity gains. They also explore the economics of intelligence, including why the bigger shift may come not from smarter individual agents, but from AI agents learning to coordinate at scale.
episodes.title: Alex Imas & Tyler Cowen | AI Is Moving Fast. Why Isn’t the Economy?
episodes.why: DeepMind economist Alex Imas and Tyler Cowen on why fast AI has not meant fast growth yet - bottlenecks, falling costs, and agents coordinating at scale.

episodes.about: Muse is the #1 app in the App Store and arguably the fastest-growing AI consumer product of all time. Mona Sarantakos has led product on it since day one. She is VP of Product at Meta Superintelligence Labs and a 10-year Meta veteran with over 20 years of experience as a PM; this is her first podcast interview. They discuss how a weekend with OpenClaw on a Raspberry Pi turned into Muse, why Muse waited seven months to launch despite getting started before most competitors, how Nat Friedman, Alex Wang, and Mark Zuckerberg each left their imprint on the product, how the team uses agent swarms to surface user insights at scale, the use case nobody on the team predicted, and the two levers that actually move activation for an AI agent.
episodes.title: Meta’s Muse: How we launched the most successful consumer product this year | Mona Sarantakos
episodes.why: Mona Sarantakos's first interview on building Meta's Muse - the #1 app in the App Store - from a Raspberry Pi weekend project and a seven-month wait to launch.

episodes.about: What do AI-native companies actually do differently? Drawing on examples from Stripe, Shopify, Uber, Ramp, and others, NLW breaks down seven practices that turn agents into useful systems - from shared company context and automatically triggered work to verification and human accountability. Plus, why the AI teammate model may be giving way to something more effective: flexible groups of agents organized around the work, rather than a fixed roster of digital coworkers.
episodes.title: 7 Things AI-Native Companies Do Differently
episodes.why: NLW's seven practices from Stripe, Shopify, Uber and Ramp for turning agents into useful systems - and why the fixed AI teammate model is fading.

episodes.about: AI adoption in businesses continues to tick up - but not as much as before, according to a recent report from expense management platform Ramp. What's News host Luke Vargas speaks with Ara Kharazian, lead economist at Ramp, about what the latest data tells us about the state of the AI market. Julie Chang hosts.
episodes.title: The Era of Unchecked Corporate AI Spending Is Over
episodes.why: Ramp's latest spending data in 11 minutes: corporate AI adoption is still rising, but the unchecked-spending phase is over.

episodes.about: Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO shook Silicon Valley to its core and sent ripples across global markets. Lauren Goode, WIRED senior correspondent who has closely followed Jensen's rise and surprising fall and has interviewed him over the years, joins Katie to make sense of this seismic news, drawing on her earlier interviews with Huang on Nvidia hardware and his plan to make AI the new world infrastructure.
episodes.title: This Isn’t The Last We Will Hear from Jensen Huang
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Uncanny Valley is WIRED's show on tech colliding with politics and business: Lauren Goode, who has interviewed Jensen Huang for years, on why his exit is not the end of his story.
